texts: good. the Cove's former role is recorded both as a dated state (six generations before now) and as a plain 'the Sunken Cove was a graveyard' fact, with the village's claim on it kept.
good. everything lands — the surge, the water it drove, the cliff edge as part of the cliff, the 'over' path, the past tense and the six-generations-ago timing.
good. the surge is the actor, the graveyard is the thing moved, and 'into the inlet' is recorded as where the washing ended up.

mixed: the group-level facts are right — both the bodies and the markers settled, in the past, at the bottom of the Sunken Cove, with the bottom tied to the Cove — but the parse omits the per-member rules, so a particular body or marker named in a later sentence could not be shown to have settled there. No rewrite would help here: the wording is already the pattern our instruction set legislates for a definite plural with a distributive verb, so the missing rules are a translator-side omission that a re-parse should supply.
good. the villagers' view is recorded without asserting that the storm-surge really was Aelmere's original misfortune, and the view is carried down to each villager as well as to the group.
